system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: VITAL NCT01169259 - Vitamin D and Omega-3 Trial (VITAL)
Investigational drug: omega-3 fatty acids
Document: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01169259 VITAL (registry, published 2010-07-26, source ctgov:NCT01169259@2018-11-10)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT01169259 (VITAL)
Title: Vitamin D and Omega-3 Trial (VITAL)
Official title: Vitamin D and Omega-3 Trial (VITAL)
Sponsor: Brigham and Women's Hospital
Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Cancer; Cardiovascular Disease
Interventions: vitamin D3 (DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT); omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil) (DRUG); Vitamin D3 placebo (DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT); Fish oil placebo (DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT)
Start date: 2010-07
Enrollment: 25871 (ACTUAL)
Primary outcome(s): Number of Participants With Invasive Cancer of Any Type [5 years] | Number of Participants With a Major Cardiovascular Event [5 years]
Eligibility criteria:
To be eligible for the study, respondents had to, at study entry,:

1. be men aged 50 or older or women aged 55 or older;
2. have no history of cancer (except non-melanoma skin cancer), heart attack, stroke, transient ischemic attack, angina pectoris, coronary-artery bypass grafting, or percutaneous coronary intervention;
3. have none of the following safety exclusions: history of renal failure or dialysis, hypercalcemia, hypo- or hyperparathyroidism, severe liver disease (cirrhosis), or sarcoidosis or other granulomatous diseases such as active chronic tuberculosis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's);
4. have no allergy to fish or soy;
5. have no other serious illness that would preclude participation;
6. be consuming no more than 800 IU of vitamin D from all supplemental sources combined (individual vitamin D supplements, calcium+vitamin D supplements, medications with vitamin D \[e.g., Fosamax Plus D\], and multivitamins), or, if taking, willing to decrease or forego such use during the trial;
7. be consuming no more than 1200 mg/d of calcium from all supplemental sources combined, or, if taking, willing to decrease or forego such use during the trial;
8. not be taking fish oil supplements, or, if taking, willing to forego their use during the trial
Brief summary: The VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL) is a randomized clinical trial in 25,871 U.S. men and women investigating whether taking daily dietary supplements of vitamin D3 (2000 IU) or omega-3 fatty acids (Omacor® fish oil, 1 gram) reduces the risk of developing cancer, heart disease, and stroke in people who do not have a prior history of these illnesses. The 5-year intervention phase (study pill-taking, median 5.3 years) has ended; post-intervention observational follow-up of study participants is ongoing.
--- END ---
